title: The 14 sweep flags in your paragraphs
intro: On 12 October I checked sections 1 to 12 against the published article for three kinds of break: an "it" or vaguer word where the original names something, a narrower thing in place of a general one, and a dropped word that sets a standard or says how long something holds. 14 of its 18 flags landed in your own paragraphs. For each: "You meant it" (a change you made on purpose, so the check should leave your choices alone), "Same meaning" (the check is wrong, and I fix the check), or "Fix it" (a real mistake: I fix the text). Two of them (F4 and F6) contain my words, which you approved.
